title: Stabilize the atmosphere-sky e2e: deterministic aim, confirmed pre-fix FAIL + 3x post-fix PASS
description: Picks up TASK-76 where attempt 2 left it. The far-plane fix (TASK-76 step 1: `CAMERA_FAR = 4000` in `app/src/client/world/WorldManager.ts`) and the unit test (step 2) are COMMITTED and green; the e2e repro was confirmed to FAIL pre-fix (central top band mean = 0.0, two runs). The one remaining blocker is that the aim loop in `app/tests/e2e/atmosphere-sky.spec.ts` is flaky: it yaws the ship at the dome anchor via the flight model for a fixed 14 iterations holding `w` (thrust) at 60 u altitude, which changes altitude/pitch, and once ended 174.7° off (that run read central band 0.0 post-fix). This task makes the aim deterministic, re-confirms the spec FAILS with the old far plane (1000 u) and records the measured value, and confirms 3 consecutive post-fix passes. It does NOT run the full verification matrix — that is TASK-76.2.

steps.description: Rewrite the aim block in app/tests/e2e/atmosphere-sky.spec.ts to be deterministic
steps.details: The aim block is ~lines 299-352 (from `--- Aim the nose at the dome ANCHOR ---` through the `aimed at the anchor` console.log). Replace the steering logic: (a) yaw WITHOUT holding `w` — safe because the server's yaw is thrust-independent (`app/src/shared/physics/flight.ts` ~line 261: `input.yaw * cls.turnRate * h` is applied unconditionally; `w`/thrust only adds velocity); (b) loop against a wall-clock deadline (~8-10 s) instead of a fixed iteration count, each iteration: probe heading error via the existing `aimProbe`, press `d` or `a` (sign calibrated as today with the one 120 ms calibration press, also without `w`) for a duration proportional to |err|; (c) HARD-ASSERT convergence before measuring: after the loop, log the final heading error and `expect(Math.abs(err)).toBeLessThan(0.12)` with an explicit message — the test must fail loudly rather than silently measure with the nose pointing the wrong way; (d) keep the existing re-pin teleport after the aim (it restores the exact spot; teleport preserves orientation — verified in shard.teleportForTesting). Do NOT change the target choice (densest seeded atmosphere), the teleport offset ladder, the TOP_BAND constants, the assertion, or the screenshot path.

steps.description: Re-confirm the spec FAILS with the old far plane (1000 u)
steps.details: Temporarily edit `app/src/client/world/WorldManager.ts` so the constructor uses `new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(70, 1, 0.1, 1000)` (revert only that one argument; leave `CAMERA_FAR` exported). Run `cd app && npx playwright test --config playwright.e2e.config.ts atmosphere-sky`. Expect FAIL: the central top band mean must be <= 5 (the two earlier pre-fix runs read exactly 0.0 with the old spec; with the fixed aim the ship faces the clipped cap deterministically so this should be as dark or darker). Record the measured mean. Then restore the file EXACTLY to its committed state: `git checkout -- app/src/client/world/WorldManager.ts` and verify with `git diff -- app/src/client/world/WorldManager.ts` that it is empty. This proves the FINAL form of the spec catches the bug.

With `CAMERA_FAR = 4000` restored, run `cd app && npx playwright test --config playwright.e2e.config.ts atmosphere-sky` THREE times — the config has retries: 0, so every run must pass on its own (each run boots its own dev server, ~1-2 min overhead; the test sets a 150 s timeout). Each run must log: heading error < 0.12 rad, central top band mean > 5 (expect ~150: ocean haze tint #6fa8dc, luminance ~160, at haze ~0.93), bright >> 0, regime=atmosphere. LOOK at `.ralph/screenshots/TASK-76-1.png` after the last run: it must show a hazy blue sky, NOT black. If a run fails, debug the aim (steering loop, deadlines, probe timing) — the geometry is verified correct (aiming at the anchor IS the clipped cap; the cap spans ~67° from the nose at 794 u from the anchor, the central strip spans only ~14-38°), do NOT loosen the assertion or the TOP_BAND region.

`cd app && npx tsc --noEmit` (the tsconfig includes `tests/`, so the spec is type-checked). `npx vitest run src/client/world/world-manager.test.ts` (must stay 10/10 green — guard against accidentally touching the constants). Commit with message `wip(TASK-76): deterministic atmosphere-sky e2e aim; pre-fix FAIL re-confirmed (central band mean <X>), 3/3 post-fix passes (~<Y>)`. The commit must contain ONLY `app/tests/e2e/atmosphere-sky.spec.ts` (and the updated screenshot `.ralph/screenshots/TASK-76-1.png` if it changed). Update `.ralph/handoff/TASK-76.md` to reflect the new state (aim fixed, values recorded) and include it in the commit. Do NOT commit the pre-existing dirty files: `ralph.config.json`, `.ralph/screenshots/TASK-28.1-1.png`, `TASK-70-1.png`, `TASK-72-1.png`, `TASK-73-1.png` — check `git status --short` before committing.

acceptanceCriteria: The aim block yaws without thrust, loops against a wall-clock deadline, and hard-asserts |heading error| < 0.12 rad before any measurement (no silent mis-aim)
With the old far plane (constructor arg 1000) the spec FAILS: central top band mean <= 5; the measured value is recorded in the commit message and the handoff
With CAMERA_FAR = 4000, three consecutive runs PASS: central top band mean > 5 (expected ~150), bright >> 0, regime 'atmosphere'; .ralph/screenshots/TASK-76-1.png shows a hazy blue sky, not black
`npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `world-manager.test.ts` still 10/10 green, one commit containing only the spec (and handoff/screenshot), pre-existing dirty files untouched

THE E2E FLOW (already in the spec, do not rebuild it): densestAtmosphericPad('DRIFT-SEED-0001') re-derives the seeded galaxy with the SAME shared code the server uses (RELATIVE imports — the Playwright runner does not resolve tsconfig aliases) → system 9f065b79f5c34fd3 (ocean, density 0.0985, pad (20170, 229.0, 195)) → raw REST claim → raw WS warp to that system (pvp-kill.spec.ts pattern; the router validates the warp target only against the seed, NOT the chart neighbor list) → browser joins via ?sys= → chase camera armed (__SELF_SHIP__.probe().screen) → dev-teleport 600 u off the pad at 60 u LOCAL altitude (terrain re-derived with generateSurfaceChunk) → offset ladder [600, 450, 300, 150] until probe().pos within 50 u AND server regime 'atmosphere' (entity_update tap) → AIM (this task) → re-pin teleport → measure.

BAND GEOMETRY (why the assertion is a CENTRAL strip TOP_BAND {x0:0.35, y0:0, x1:0.65, y1:0.3}): pre-fix the clipped dome cap (black) sits in the view CENTRE, ringed by the VISIBLE part of the dome (within the 1000 u far plane) — a bright-blue ring reaching the corners. A full-width band false-passes pre-fix (mean 51). The central strip stays inside the clipped cap (cap spans ~67° from the nose at 794 u from the anchor; the strip spans only ~14-38°). The full-width band is still logged, not asserted.

DEAD ENDS (do not retry): (1) full-width top band as the assertion region — false-passes pre-fix; (2) the home system's pad — atmosphere too thin (density ~0.06 → haze ~0.6 at 60 u → band stays bright, bug invisible); (3) keyboardWarp to the densest system — the chart only exposes neighbors, use the raw WS warp already in the spec; (4) the old aim loop (14 fixed iterations holding `w`) — observed heading errors 4.2°, 14.9° (ok) and 174.7° (FAILED, band read 0.0 post-fix).

RECORDED VALUES: pre-fix (2 runs, old spec): central top band mean = 0.0, bright = 0 — this is the failing value the LOG.md entry (TASK-76.2) records. Post-fix expectation: central band mean ~150 (ocean haze tint #6fa8dc, luminance ~160, at haze ~0.93; haze = (1 - alt/1000) x min(1, density/0.1) from hazeFactor in @shared/physics/atmosphere). Facts: dome radius 1000 x 1.01 = 1010 u; pad sits ~260 u off its planet anchor so 600 u pad-offset = ~794 u from the anchor; far wall 1804 u, clipped by the old 1000 u plane; sky radius 420 u (TASK-75 keeps it camera-centred); sky top #131f33 (lum ~30).

ENVIRONMENT: e2e config app/playwright.e2e.config.ts — workers 1, retries 0 (each run must pass on its own; the handoff's 'retries:1' note is wrong), globalTimeout 15 min, atmosphere-sky sets its own 150 s timeout. Headless SwiftShader GL renders fine (no launch flags needed). Each spec file boots its own dev server via tests/e2e/fixtures.ts (~1-2 min overhead per run). Run command: `cd app && npx playwright test --config playwright.e2e.config.ts atmosphere-sky`.

Do NOT change the dome radius, the haze math or the crossfade — the shared atmosphere math is correct; only the camera could not see the whole dome. The mobile flat-haze layer (createFlatHaze) uses the same radius, so the same far plane fixes it too.
